note: About the icon a browser shows for a web page. An app sets its window and tray icons itself.
An icon node draws SVG markup or an `.svg` file with lib-svg: shapes, paths, text, gradients, patterns, clipping, masks and markers.
In icons: lib-svg draws `<filter>` elements with every primitive.
App text cannot use SVG fonts: `@font-face` does not load them. Inside an icon's markup, lib-svg draws the document's own `<font>` elements.
An icon draws its whole document; a `#id` or `#svgView(...)` fragment in its URL does not pick out a part.

Nodes cannot use SVG effects by reference: `filter: url(#id)` is skipped, `clip-path: url(#id)` clips to the border box, and there is no `foreignObject` for nodes. CSS filter functions, shapes and gradient masks work.

An icon takes SVG markup as a string (`createIcon(svg)`, `<icon svg={...}>` in React) and draws it with the node's `color` as `currentColor`. The SVG elements are not tree nodes, so app stylesheets, events and scripts do not reach inside it.
An `.svg` file loads by URL into an icon node. An image node decodes PNG and JPEG, not SVG.
SMIL and CSS animations inside an icon play, rendered per frame. Good for small icons such as spinners; each frame is a separate texture.
